verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — X wins on two material wrong claims in Y that I refuted against the code. (1) Y says `${f}.count` is "Reset to absent only by an explicit CLI `set` (:142)"; `hooks/session-continue.sh:1206` removes `.count` on every unarmed Stop before `mechanical_arm` is called, and `:1260` removes it at the cap — which is exactly why the mechanical bound is the PRODUCT Y itself quotes from `:1046-1048`. (2) Y defines RUNG=🔧 by quoting the header comment at `scripts/wrap-ledger.sh:25` ("dirty ∨ gate ran-but-stale-on-HEAD ∨ remainder") as the code's behaviour; the ladder at `:1979-1982` has no gate term and `:1941-1961` is a long rationale for having removed it, while the ✅-eligible branch adds six further 🔧 sources (`:1997-2052`). X flags exactly that comment as stale. Y also attributes a two-line hook-chain.sh quote to line 78 alone (it spans :77-78), cites a nonexistent line 1345, and omits the TRUNK gate at `:1148-1149`. X additionally carries verified findings Y lacks entirely (LANDING vs ship_floor, the `:963-966` assignee-asymmetry refutation, the agent_is_assignee bypass, unsanitised caps). Y's real extras — CONTINUE_IDL/CONTINUE_LOG at `:82-83`, CC_WATCH_FRESH_S at `mailbox-pending.sh:297` — do not offset two wrong mechanism claims.

X vs Z — very close; X wins narrowly on specific verified material insights Z lacks, not on length. The decisive one: X found that the 📦 rung is set even when LANDING=1 (`wrap-ledger.sh:1985-1986`, emitted as `LANDING=` at `:2176`) while `ship_floor` greps only RUNG/TRUNK/AHEAD/SHAS — so the floor instructs "/ship it NOW" while the ledger's own readout says "do NOT fire a second /ship on this worktree". I confirmed both halves. X also uniquely establishes that `wrap-ledger.sh:25`'s 🔧 definition is stale, that the wake floor's `.wakefloor` file is keyed on the mailbox dir and NOT the config dir (unlike `.count`/`.mech`/`.ship`), that `stop_hook_active` is never read (grep: zero hits), that `set` keys on `$PWD` while actuation keys on the payload `.cwd`, and it runs negative controls on CC_TEARDOWN_DIR (`:553` vs `lead-crash-watchdog.sh:251`) and CC_MAILBOX_DIR (`:610` vs `mailbox-pending.sh:110`). Against that, X has one off-by-one inside its own stale-citation table (`:432` for a comment on `:433`) and one hedged inference error in its "not verified" section — it reasons from the memo key at `:386` and misses the four-arm SID ladder at `:636-641`, whose fourth arm is CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (`:640`). Z is essentially error-free and matches X on the assignee-comment refutation, the agent_is_assignee bypass and the bare-shell-`clear` `?` sid, and is more precise on mailbox_wake_armed's no-pid branch — but its unique additions are smaller than X's four.

Y vs Z — Z wins. Z carries no material wrong claim I could find over ~38 checked citations; its only blemishes are a one-line-off cite on hook-chain.sh `:24-25` and two comment-rather-than-code citations. Y carries the two mechanism errors above (`.count` reset, and the gate-stale 🔧 definition taken from a comment the code explicitly repudiates). Z also verifies things Y does not: that the arms' assignee policies are identical despite the in-file comment, that none uses agent_is_assignee's shape gate, that a bare-shell `clear` cannot spend a real session's mech budget, that CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX/CC_MECH_MAX are unsanitised, and that wf_teardown_marked omits the `"mode":"teardown"` check its own comment claims to copy verbatim.
